nodes.title: Closure points and clubs of countable subsets

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a set and let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions, each assigning an element of $X$ to every finite subset of $X$. The closure points of $(F_n)$ are the countable (finite or countably infinite) sets $x \subseteq X$ such that $F_n(s) \in x$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every finite set $s \subseteq x$.
nodes.title: Closure points of a sequence of finitary functions

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a set and let $F$ be a function assigning an element of $X$ to every finite subset of $X$. The closure points of $F$ are the countable (finite or countably infinite) sets $a \subseteq X$ such that $F(s) \in a$ for every finite set $s \subseteq a$.
nodes.title: Closure points of a finitary function

nodes.summary: A set X⊆κ is *bounded in κ* if there is some β<κ with α<β for every α∈ X; equivalently, X⊆β for some β<κ.
nodes.title: Family containing all bounded subsets of a cardinal

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a set. A family $C$ of subsets of $X$ is club in the countable subsets of $X$ when every member of $C$ is countable (finite or countably infinite), every countable set $x \subseteq X$ is contained in some member of $C$, and for every sequence $x_0 \subseteq x_1 \subseteq x_2 \subseteq \cdots$ of members of $C$ the union $\bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} x_n$ belongs to $C$.
nodes.title: Club families of countable sets

nodes.summary: Let $\kappa$ be a cardinal, identified with its initial ordinal, let $S$ be a set of ordinals less than $\kappa$, and let $f$ be a function from $S$ to the ordinals less than $\kappa$. Then $f$ is regressive if $f(\alpha) < \alpha$ for every nonzero $\alpha \in S$.
nodes.title: Regressive functions

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a set. A family $S$ of subsets of $X$ is stationary in the countable subsets of $X$ when $S$ meets every family $C$ that is club in the countable subsets of $X$, that is, some set belongs to both $S$ and $C$.
nodes.title: Stationary families of countable sets
